text:
Detroit arrives winless in four and 1-4-0 in its last five, coming off a 3-2 loss at St. Louis, and it's missing Dylan Larkin (suspended) and Albert Johansson. Florida, 2-3-0 over the same stretch, won 4-1 at Columbus on Tuesday but is without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand. Detroit won the first meeting 5-3 on November 2, which makes this a rematch between two banged-up teams.

The numbers say these teams are close. Each has taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, and our model has Florida slightly ahead tonight, 3.25 expected goals to 2.94. Detroit's recent slide is real: it has had only 43% of the chances during its winless run. The special-teams gap favors Florida, whose power play creates 1.17 expected goals a game against 0.82 for Detroit's. Florida also takes 5.7 penalties a game, though, which keeps handing out power plays.

In net, John Gibson is projected for Detroit and has been 6.1 goals worse than expected this season (after a plus-10.1 last year). Akira Schmid is projected for Florida at plus 0.5. With Marchand and Barkov out, Matthew Tkachuk has moved onto a line beside Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk, and he's on a five-game point streak. Reinhart, two points shy of 700 for his career, has our highest goal probability at 40%. For Detroit, Viktor Arvidsson has gone six games without a goal on 2.5 expected, and we give him a 33% chance to end it.
